question.problem:
The equation of the hyperbola $14{x}^{2}-21{y}^{2}=126$ in standard form is{{field-1}}
$=1.$
question.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin is

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

Therefore, to write the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to divide both sides of the equation by $126$ and then simplify, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}14{x}^{2}-21{y}^{2} & =126 \\ \frac{14{x}^{2}}{126}-\frac{21{y}^{2}}{126} & =\frac{126}{126} \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{9}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{6} & =1\end{aligned}
$$
